text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The state budget was approved with 62 votes in favour. Right-wing parties voted against it.

- State-run and privately-owned radio stations are in a row over the right to celebrate the 70th anniversary of broadcasting in Estonia. A private station which began broadcasting in December 1926 was nationalised in 1934.

- Russian MPs visiting Estonia want to link ratification of the border agreement with planned NATO enlargement and the situation of the Russian-speaking population in Estonia. They acknowledge that some progress in minority issues has been made.

- Parliamentary Foreign Affairs Commission head Eino Tamm claims that the Russian expert delegation visiting Estonia last week operated under the orders of the Russian Foreign Ministry and their findings will be used against Estonia by politicians.
- Metal processsing plant Silmet in Sillamae may be sold to a corporation EPHAG, jointly owned by Estonian businessmen and an American bank.
- A special foundation will be formed for the "Tiger's Leap" national computerisation programme in order to coordinate funding.
- A confusion with exports to Ukraine has been successfully solved and the recently introduced higher tariffs will not apply to Estonian-produced goods.
